I never read this when it came out, so here I am, like, 40 years later, catching up. [I was neck deep in quantum mechanics at the time.]
In light of all that's gone on since this book was written, it's a jumble of ideas, some old, some new, some borrowed, some hopelessly naive. Honestly, it barely has an organization, does NOT have a single point or group of related points, and is really all over the map.
McLuhan, among other things [about 11,432 of them, give or take], proposes the notions of "COLD" and "HOT" media.

Marshall McLuhan has been described as Canada's most exciting and original thinker, a member of the small company of intellectual geniuses this country has produced. Works such as The Gutenberg Galaxy , The Mechanical Bride , From Cliche to Archetype , and Understanding Media have established his reputation throughout the world and have profoundly influenced our understanding of contemporary communication. In his later years McLuhan was working on a 'unified field' theory of human culture, an effort in which he collaborated with and was assisted by his son, Eric McLuhan.
